passages.text: I ask then, did God reject His people? Certainly not! I am an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an Israelite.
Paul is a descendant of Abraham.
Paul is from the tribe of Benjamin.
The Israelites are the people of God
Paul asks if God rejected His people, the Israelites?
The answer is no!
God did not reject His people.
If God rejected all the Israelites, then Paul would have been among those rejected.
However God chose Paul, so God did not reject His people.
passages.original: Λέγω οὖν μὴ ἀπώσατο ὁ Θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ μὴ γένοιτο καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ Ἰσραηλίτης εἰμί ἐκ σπέρματος Ἀβραάμ φυλῆς Βενιαμίν

passages.text: God did not reject His people, whom He foreknew. Do you not know what the Scripture says about Elijah, how he appealed to God against Israel: “Lord, they have killed Your prophets and torn down Your altars. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well”?
passages.sermon:
God did not reject His people.
God knew His people beforehand.
Scripture speaks about Elijah.
Elijah appealed to God against Israel.
Elijah said, “Lord, they have killed Your prophets.”
Elijah said, “They have torn down Your altars.”
Elijah said, “I am the only one left.”
Elijah said, “They are seeking my life as well.”
passages.original: οὐκ ἀπώσατο ὁ Θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ὃν προέγνω ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ἐν Ἠλίᾳ τί λέγει ἡ γραφή ὡς ἐντυγχάνει τῷ Θεῷ κατὰ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ Κύριε τοὺς προφήτας σου ἀπέκτειναν τὰ θυσιαστήριά σου κατέσκαψαν κἀγὼ ὑπελείφθην μόνος καὶ ζητοῦσιν τὴν ψυχήν μου

passages.text: And what was the divine reply to him? “I have reserved for Myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Elijah.
God gave a reply to Elijah.
God said, “I have kept seven thousand men for Myself.”
These men did not bow down to Baal.
These men stayed faithful to God.
God chose and protected these seven thousand men.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ τί λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ χρηματισμός Κατέλιπον ἐμαυτῷ ἑπτακισχιλίους ἄνδρας οἵτινες οὐκ ἔκαμψαν γόνυ τῇ Βάαλ

passages.text: In the same way, at the present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.
passages.sermon:
God always keeps for Himself a remnant: a group of people faithful to Him.
God chooses His remnant by His own choice.
God does not choose His remnant by their works.
God chooses His remnant by His grace.
There was a remnant at the time of Elijah and at the time of Paul.
And there is a remnant of people today.
God has chosen us by grace.
passages.original: Οὕτως οὖν καὶ ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ λεῖμμα κατ’ ἐκλογὴν χάριτος γέγονεν

passages.text: And if it is by grace, then it is no longer by works. Otherwise, grace would no longer be grace.
passages.sermon:
God chooses people by grace.
Grace means God gives a gift.
Grace is not by works.
If God chooses by grace, then works do not decide it.
If works decide it, then it is not grace.
If works decide grace, then grace is no longer grace.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ χάριτι οὐκέτι ἐξ ἔργων ἐπεὶ ἡ χάρις οὐκέτι γίνεται χάρις

passages.text: What then? What Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain, but the elect did. The others were hardened, as it is written: “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that could not see, and ears that could not hear, to this very day.”
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks about Israel.
Israel tried to obtain something.
But Israel did not obtain it.
God chose some people called His elect.
These chosen people obtained what Israel did not obtain.
Those people who were not elect were hardened.
Scripture says God gave them a spirit of stupor.
God gave them eyes that could not see.
God gave them ears that could not hear.
This continues to this very day.
passages.original: Τί οὖν ὃ ἐπιζητεῖ Ἰσραήλ τοῦτο οὐκ ἐπέτυχεν ἡ δὲ ἐκλογὴ ἐπέτυχεν οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ ἐπωρώθησαν καθὼς γέγραπται Ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς πνεῦμα κατανύξεως ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν καὶ ὦτα τοῦ μὴ ἀκούειν ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας

passages.text: And David says: “May their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution to them.
passages.sermon:
David speaks in Psalms.
David asks for judgment on certain people.
David asks that their table become a snare.
David asks that their table become to become a trap.
David asks that their table become to a stumbling block.
David asks that their table become to a retribution to them.
passages.original: Καὶ Δαυὶδ λέγει Γενηθήτω ἡ τράπεζα αὐτῶν εἰς παγίδα καὶ εἰς θήραν καὶ εἰς σκάνδαλον καὶ εἰς ἀνταπόδομα αὐτοῖς

passages.text: May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.”
passages.sermon:
David speaks about those who reject God.
David asks God to darken their eyes.
David asks God to keep their eyes from seeing.
David asks God to bend their backs always.
passages.original: σκοτισθήτωσαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν καὶ τὸν νῶτον αὐτῶν διὰ παντὸς σύνκαμψον

passages.text: I ask then, did they stumble so as to fall beyond recovery? Certainly not! However, because of their trespass, salvation has come to the Gentiles to make Israel jealous.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking about the people of Israel.
Paul asks a question about Israel.
Paul asks: Did Israel stumble so that they would fall forever?
Paul answers, “Certainly not!”
The Israelites will not fall forever.
Instead of falling forever, one day the Israelites will accept Jesus.
However, because Israel sinned, salvation came to the Gentiles.
God did this to make Israel jealous.
passages.original: Λέγω οὖν μὴ ἔπταισαν ἵνα πέσωσιν μὴ γένοιτο ἀλλὰ τῷ αὐτῶν παραπτώματι ἡ σωτηρία τοῖς ἔθνεσιν εἰς τὸ παραζηλῶσαι αὐτούς

passages.text: But if their trespass means riches for the world, and their failure means riches for the Gentiles, how much greater riches will their fullness bring!
passages.sermon:
Israel trespassed by rejecting Christ.
Because Israel rejected Christ, then the gospel and its riches went out to everyone in world.
Israel’s trespass brought riches to the world.
By rejecting Christ, Israel failed.
Israel’s failure brought riches to the Gentiles.
If Israel doing bad caused so much good, won't Israel doing good lead to even far greater good?
If Israel trespassing and failing caused so much good, won't the fullness of Israel cause even greater good and riches?
How much greater good will come from Israel accepting Jesus and being fully saved?
passages.original: εἰ δὲ τὸ παράπτωμα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος κόσμου καὶ τὸ ἥττημα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος ἐθνῶν πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῶν

passages.text: I am speaking to you Gentiles. Inasmuch as I am the apostle to the Gentiles, I magnify my ministry in the hope that I may provoke my own people to jealousy and save some of them.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Gentiles.
Paul is the apostle to the Gentiles.
Paul honors his ministry.
Paul hopes his fellow Jewish people become aware of the work God is doing among the Gentiles.
Paul hopes that these Jews will be jealous of the blessings in Christ that God has given the Gentiles.
Paul hopes these Jews will want to participate in Christ and receive these blessings.
Paul wants these jealous Jews to come to Christ and be saved.
passages.original: Ὑμῖν δὲ λέγω τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἐφ’ ὅσον μὲν οὖν εἰμι ἐγὼ ἐθνῶν ἀπόστολος τὴν διακονίαν μου δοξάζω εἴ πως παραζηλώσω μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ σώσω τινὰς ἐξ αὐτῶν

passages.text: For if their rejection is the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?
passages.sermon:
God rejected the people of Israel for a time.
Their rejection brought reconciliation to the world.
God made peace with the world through this rejection.
When God accepts Israel again, something abundantly great will happen.
God rejecting Israel was like a death.
And so God accepting Israel will be like life from the dead.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ ἡ ἀποβολὴ αὐτῶν καταλλαγὴ κόσμου τίς ἡ πρόσλημψις εἰ μὴ ζωὴ ἐκ νεκρῶν

passages.text: If the first part of the dough is holy, so is the whole batch; if the root is holy, so are the branches.
passages.sermon:
As an analogy, suppose someone is baking dough.
Suppose the first part of the dough is holy.
Then the whole batch of dough is holy.
And as another analogy, suppose there is a tree.
Suppose the root of the tree is holy.
Then the branches of the tree are also holy.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ἡ ἀπαρχὴ ἁγία καὶ τὸ φύραμα καὶ εἰ ἡ ῥίζα ἁγία καὶ οἱ κλάδοι

passages.text: Now if some branches have been broken off, and you, a wild olive shoot, have been grafted in among the others to share in the nourishment of the olive root, do not boast over those branches. If you do, remember this: You do not support the root, but the root supports you.
passages.sermon:
As an analogy, there is a tree with branches that represents the people of God.
God rejected some Jews as His people and thus some branches were broken off this tree.
If someone is a Gentile, then they are a wild olive shoot.
If this Gentile accepts Christ, then they been grafted into the tree among the other branches.
That Gentile now shares in the nourishment of the olive root.
That Gentile must not boast over those rejected natural branches.
If someone boasts, remember this.
None of us supports the root.
The root supports us.
passages.original: Εἰ δέ τινες τῶν κλάδων ἐξεκλάσθησαν σὺ δὲ ἀγριέλαιος ὢν ἐνεκεντρίσθης ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ συνκοινωνὸς τῆς ῥίζης τῆς πιότητος τῆς ἐλαίας ἐγένου μὴ κατακαυχῶ τῶν κλάδων εἰ δὲ κατακαυχᾶσαι οὐ σὺ τὴν ῥίζαν βαστάζεις ἀλλὰ ἡ ῥίζα σέ

passages.text: You will say then, “Branches were broken off so that I could be grafted in.”
passages.sermon:
When God rejected some Jews, then some branches were broken off from the cultivated olive tree of the people of God.
Gentiles are a wild olive shoots.
Gentiles were grafted in among the remaining branches.
A Gentile may say, “Branches were broken off so that I could be grafted in.”
passages.original: Ἐρεῖς οὖν Ἐξεκλάσθησαν κλάδοι ἵνα ἐγὼ ἐγκεντρισθῶ

passages.text: That is correct: They were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not be arrogant, but be afraid.
passages.sermon:
It is correct that the Jews God rejected from the tree of the people of God so that Gentile wild olive shoots could be grafted into the tree.
However, those Jews were broken off because of unbelief.
And Gentiles stand by faith.
Gentiles must not be arrogant.
Gentiles must fear.
passages.original: καλῶς τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἐξεκλάσθησαν σὺ δὲ τῇ πίστει ἕστηκας μὴ ὑψηλὰ φρόνει ἀλλὰ φοβοῦ

passages.text: For if God did not spare the natural branches, He will certainly not spare you either.
passages.sermon:
The natural branches are the original people of Israel.
God did not spare the natural branches.
God judged these natural branches because of their unbelief.
If a Gentile does not continue in faith, God will not spare them, either.
Because God is just to everyone, God will not spare anyone—Jew or Gentile—who does not continue in faith.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς τῶν κατὰ φύσιν κλάδων οὐκ ἐφείσατο μή πως οὐδὲ σοῦ φείσεται

passages.text: Take notice, therefore, of the kindness and severity of God: severity to those who fell, but kindness to you, if you continue in His kindness. Otherwise you also will be cut off.
passages.sermon:
God shows kindness.
God shows severity.
God shows both kindness and severity.
God showed severity to those who fell.
God shows kindness to us.
However, we must continue in God’s kindness.
If we do not continue in God’s kindness, then God will also cut us off.
passages.original: ἴδε οὖν χρηστότητα καὶ ἀποτομίαν Θεοῦ ἐπὶ μὲν τοὺς πεσόντας ἀποτομία ἐπὶ δὲ σὲ χρηστότης Θεοῦ ἐὰν ἐπιμένῃς τῇ χρηστότητι ἐπεὶ καὶ σὺ ἐκκοπήσῃ

passages.text: And if they do not persist in unbelief, they will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.
passages.sermon:
God has power to graft people in again.
If someone does not continue in unbelief, God will graft them in.
God can restore someone who did not believe.
passages.original: κἀκεῖνοι δέ ἐὰν μὴ ἐπιμένωσιν τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἐνκεντρισθήσονται δυνατὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ Θεὸς πάλιν ἐνκεντρίσαι αὐτούς

passages.text: For if you were cut from a wild olive tree, and contrary to nature were grafted into one that is cultivated, how much more readily will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree!
passages.sermon:
God is able to graft people into His family.
Gentiles were not a natural part of God’s chosen people.
God cut each Gentile from a wild olive tree.
God grafted each Gentile into a cultivated olive tree.
God grafting Gentiles was not natural.
God grafting Gentiles by His power and grace.
The natural branches are the people of Israel.
The natural branches belong to the cultivated olive tree by nature.
God can graft the natural branches back into their own olive tree.
The natural branches are grafted in more easily than the wild branches.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ σὺ ἐκ τῆς κατὰ φύσιν ἐξεκόπης ἀγριελαίου καὶ παρὰ φύσιν ἐνεκεντρίσθης εἰς καλλιέλαιον πόσῳ μᾶλλον οὗτοι οἱ κατὰ φύσιν ἐνκεντρισθήσονται τῇ ἰδίᾳ ἐλαίᾳ

passages.text: I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, brothers, so that you will not be conceited: A hardening in part has come to Israel, until the full number of the Gentiles has come in.
passages.sermon:
God has allowed a partial hardening to come upon Israel.
This hardening will last for a time.
This hardening will continue until the full number of the Gentiles has come in.
This is a mystery.
Paul did not want the brothers he was writing to to be ignorant of this mystery.
We should not be ignorant of this mystery, either.
Therefore Gentiles should not be conceited that they are grafted into the tree of God's people over a natural branch.
passages.original: Οὐ γὰρ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν ἀδελφοί τὸ μυστήριον τοῦτο ἵνα μὴ ἦτε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς φρόνιμοι ὅτι πώρωσις ἀπὸ μέρους τῷ Ἰσραὴλ γέγονεν ἄχρι οὗ τὸ πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰσέλθῃ

passages.text: And so all Israel will be saved, as it is written: “The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will remove godlessness from Jacob.
passages.sermon:
God promises to save all Israel.
The Deliverer will come from Zion.
The Deliverer will remove godlessness from Jacob.
Scripture says this in Isaiah.
passages.original: καὶ οὕτως πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ σωθήσεται καθὼς γέγραπται Ἥξει ἐκ Σιὼν ὁ Ῥυόμενος ἀποστρέψει ἀσεβείας ἀπὸ Ἰακώβ

passages.text: And this is My covenant with them when I take away their sins.”
passages.sermon:
God made a covenant with Israel.
In the covenant God made with Israel, God promised to take away all the sins of Israel.
passages.original: καὶ αὕτη αὐτοῖς ἡ παρ’ ἐμοῦ διαθήκη ὅταν ἀφέλωμαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν

passages.text: Regarding the gospel, they are enemies on your account; but regarding election, they are loved on account of the patriarchs.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel who rejected Jesus are enemies of the gospel for our sake.
However, God loves the people of Israel who rejected Jesus.
Regarding God's election, God loves all the Israelites - even those who rejected Jesus.
On account of the patriarchs, God loves all the Jews, including those who rejected Jesus.
passages.original: Κατὰ μὲν τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἐχθροὶ δι’ ὑμᾶς κατὰ δὲ τὴν ἐκλογὴν ἀγαπητοὶ διὰ τοὺς πατέρας

passages.text: For God’s gifts and His call are irrevocable.
passages.sermon:
God gives gifts.
God calls people.
God does not change His mind when He gives a gift.
God does not change His mind after He calls.
God does not take back His gifts.
God does not take back His call.
God’s gifts last forever.
God’s call lasts forever.
passages.original: ἀμεταμέλητα γὰρ τὰ χαρίσματα καὶ ἡ κλῆσις τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Just as you who formerly disobeyed God have now received mercy through their disobedience, so they too have now disobeyed, in order that they too may now receive mercy through the mercy shown to you.
passages.sermon:
As Gentile believers, you once disobeyed God.
Now God has given you mercy.
God gave you mercy because of the disobedience of the Jews.
And now the Jews have disobeyed God.
God will give the Jews mercy because of the mercy He gave to you.
God wants the Jews to receive mercy now.
passages.original: Ὥσπερ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ποτε ἠπειθήσατε τῷ Θεῷ νῦν δὲ ἠλεήθητε τῇ τούτων ἀπειθείᾳ οὕτως καὶ οὗτοι νῦν ἠπείθησαν τῷ ὑμετέρῳ ἐλέει ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ νῦν ἐλεηθῶσιν

passages.text: For God has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone.
passages.sermon:
God has placed all people under disobedience.
God did this so He can have mercy on all people.
passages.original: συνέκλεισεν γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς τοὺς πάντας εἰς ἀπείθειαν ἵνα τοὺς πάντας ἐλεήσῃ

passages.text: O, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments, and untraceable His ways!
passages.sermon:
God is rich in wisdom.
God is rich in knowledge.
The riches of the wisdom of God are deep.
The riches of the knowledge of God are deep.
No one can search out God’s judgments.
No one can trace God’s ways.
passages.original: Ὦ βάθος πλούτου καὶ σοφίας καὶ γνώσεως Θεοῦ ὡς ἀνεξεραύνητα τὰ κρίματα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνεξιχνίαστοι αἱ ὁδοὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: “Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counselor?”
passages.sermon:
No one fully understands the mind of the Lord.
The mind of God knows everything, whereas we only know in part.
No one has ever been the Lord’s counselor.
No one gives advice to God.
passages.original: Τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν Κυρίου ἢ τίς σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο

passages.text: “Who has first given to God, that God should repay him?”
passages.sermon:
No one has given anything to God first where then God pays them back.
Rather, first God gives to us, and then we give back to God what He first gave us.
God is the First and the Last.
passages.original: Ἢ τίς προέδωκεν αὐτῷ καὶ ἀνταποδοθήσεται αὐτῷ

passages.text: For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever! Amen.
passages.sermon:
God is the source of all things.
God works through all things.
All things exist for God.
God, to You we give the glory forever!
Amen!
passages.original: ὅτι ἐξ αὐτοῦ καὶ δι’ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰς αὐτὸν τὰ πάντα αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας ἀμήν
